about: The Benedic, Domine is a short blessing before a meal. Those gathered ask the Lord to bless both them and the gifts they are about to receive from his bounty, making the petition through Christ.

translation_citations.title: Francis X. Lasance, The Catholic Girl's Guide (1906)

s03.translation: which we are about to receive from your bounty.

w001.function: The imperative opens a direct petition to the Lord and governs two coordinated objects: “nos” and “hæc tua dona”.

w002.function: The vocative identifies the Lord as the prayer's sole addressee.

w003.function: The first direct object of “Bénedic” comprises the community of speakers.

w004.function: The conjunction joins persons and gifts as coordinate objects of one blessing.

w005.function: The demonstrative agrees with “dona” and points to the gifts present at the meal.

w006.function: The possessive relates the gifts to the Lord addressed in the prayer.

w007.function: The second direct object of “Bénedic”, coordinated with “nos”.

w008.function: The relative resumes neuter “dona” and serves as the object of the participle “sumptúri” in the predicate with “sumus”.

w009.function: The preposition with the ablative marks the source of the gifts received.

w011.function: The ablative after “de” names divine bounty as the source of the gifts.

w012.function: With “sumptúri”, the auxiliary forms a first-person plural future active periphrastic.

w013.function: The future active participle agrees with the understood human speakers and, with “sumus”, expresses imminent reception.

w015.function: The accusative governed by “Per” expresses Christ's mediation in the prayer's conclusion.

w017.function: The adjective agrees with “Dóminum” and includes the same community that spoke as “nos” and “sumus”.
